title: Stratabox: Reserve Decision Hub — compact ops cockpit for burst & autoscale
creator: Maya Chen
description: Design and prototype a compact decision hub for Redwood Console that surfaces GPU reserve health, autoscale intent, and burst controls in a single, glancable card. The Stratabox is intended for SREs and platform engineers who need quick, low-friction actions (adjust target capacity, trigger burst, set hysteresis) plus an immediate cost/latency preview before applying changes. This ticket covers component specs, accessibility, interaction states, and a high-fidelity prototype for PM/Eng review.
acceptance_criteria: High-fidelity prototype (desktop) demonstrating: health summary, real-time sparkline, autoscale slider with presets, burst budget quick-trigger, and cost-latency delta modal
Component specs (tokens, spacing, color, states) published to the design system library
Edge cases documented: offline metrics, read-only user, concurrent override conflicts
Engineering sign-off on telemetry hooks (events for preview, apply, rollback) and API surface for optimistic UI
Usability validation: 5/5 target users can complete common tasks in < 60s in moderated testing
design_notes: Card-first pattern: compact header (pool name + status pill) with expand-to-panel for detailed timeline
Health summary uses a 3-tier severity with micro-sparkline (60m/6h/24h toggles). Colors mapped to system-wide tokens (green/amber/red) and an additional 'degraded' amber-muted for noisy spikes
Autoscale control is a two-mode input: Preset dropdown (conservative/standard/aggressive) + fine-grained slider for immediate adjustments. Slider shows projected TPS and 95p latency at knob position
Burst quick-trigger uses a budget-aware modal: shows token cost estimate, duration, and automatic retraction policy. Defaults to conservative duration (2m) unless operator escalates
Optimistic UI pattern: preview modal calls /reserve/preview which returns cost & latency delta, UI shows ephemeral preview overlay until operator confirms
Accessibility: all controls keyboard accessible, ARIA labels for sparkline and slider, color+icon redundancy for severity
Responsive: the compact card collapses to a stack of rows on small widths; key actions remain visible (Burst / Adjust / Details)
decisions: Chose sparkline over full timeseries chart in compact state to reduce cognitive load and preserve layout density
Preview API approach (server-side estimates) to avoid inaccurate local heuristics and centralize cost model logic
Default autoscale preset set to 'standard' to balance cost/perf; advanced presets hidden behind 'Expert' toggle to avoid accidental aggressive scaling
Burst triggers require a two-step confirmation when budget > 5000 token-equivalent to avoid costly mistakes
No inline editing of hysteresis values in compact view — moved to expanded panel to prevent accidental toggles
tradeoffs: Density vs discoverability: single-card view keeps dashboard tidy but hides advanced tuning. Mitigated with an 'Expand' affordance and contextual help
Realtime metrics freshness vs telemetry cost: default to 10s refresh in compact, 2s in expanded panel. Will monitor cost and raise if ingestion becomes expensive
Optimistic UI improves perceived latency but requires robust rollback and conflict resolution UX if apply fails
Cost model centralization reduces client complexity but adds an API dependency in the critical path for previews
pr_links: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1420 -- preview API endpoint and cost model integration
